landmarks.name: Rusizi National Park
landmarks.writeup: A protected area known for its hippos, crocodiles, and diverse bird species along the Rusizi River.

landmarks.name: Gishora Drum Sanctuary
landmarks.writeup: A cultural site preserving the traditional Burundian drumming heritage, central to national identity.

landmarks.name: Lake Tanganyika
landmarks.writeup: One of the African Great Lakes, it is the second deepest freshwater lake in the world and vital for fishing.

cultural_events.name: Umuganuro Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional harvest festival celebrating the start of the agricultural season with music and dance.

cultural_events.name: National Drummers Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An event showcasing Burundi's famous drumming culture, featuring performances from local and national groups.

food_writeup: Burundian cuisine is based on staple foods like beans, maize, sweet potatoes, and bananas, often accompanied by meat or fish. Ugali (a maize porridge) and isombe (cassava leaves) are popular dishes.
brief_history: Burundi, once part of the Kingdom of Burundi, became a German colony in the late 19th century, then a Belgian mandate after WWI. It gained independence in 1962. The country has experienced ethnic conflicts and civil war but continues efforts toward peace and development.
current_conflicts: Burundi faces political tensions and occasional unrest related to governance and human rights issues, but no active large-scale armed conflict.
